Tidal power comes of age at Port Hask

The Veldrin Tidal Array has now run for five full years, and its operator says the results settle an old argument about whether tidal power can be relied on.

The array's 48 seabed turbines have a combined capacity of 62 megawatts. Unlike wind, the tides are predictable decades ahead, which the operator, Norvane Energy, says makes the output unusually easy to plan around.[1]

What it cost

Construction came to 310 million crowns, about a fifth over budget, mainly because of delays laying the export cable. Critics point out that the same money would have bought considerably more wind capacity.
